name: clear_request_flag_and_reply
description: Clears bit 3 of a request block's flag byte and returns the message through exec's ReplyMsg call. When a second block is supplied, it sets that block's status byte and stores a tagged counter value in its field.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1B9C
name: mark_status_and_post_value
description: Sets the primary block's status byte to 2 and copies a status byte between fields. When one of two flags is set, it also updates the second block and writes a tagged value from the shared counter into its field.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1BF4
name: dispatch_slot_state_command
description: Dispatches on command codes 3, 4 and 5 for a four-entry slot table. Code 3 releases matching slot records, code 4 validates a slot identifier by calling a routine, and code 5 runs a routine when a global flag bit is set.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1C7E
name: check_slot_or_flag_command
description: Handles command 4 by checking that the stored slot identifier matches the current one and that a called routine accepts it, and handles command 5 by calling a routine when a global flag bit is set. Both paths write the shared result byte.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1CB6
name: clear_shared_result_byte
description: Sets the shared result byte to zero and returns success, with no other effect.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1CBE
name: run_flag_gated_action
description: Clears the shared result byte and, when command code 5 is requested and a global flag bit is set, calls a routine and sets the result byte to one. Otherwise the result stays at zero.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1CEE
name: allocate_node_with_buffer
description: Allocates a node and then a second buffer through exec's memory allocator, storing the buffer pointer in the node with two register-supplied values. When a list pointer is given it links the node into that list, and if the buffer allocation fails it frees the node and returns nothing.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1D42
name: free_indexed_list_entries
description: Detaches the linked list held in the table slot chosen by the index argument, clears that slot, and releases each entry through exec's free-memory call. Entries are walked by following the link stored in each one.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1D82
name: release_slot_record_buffers
description: Releases the two buffers attached to the slot record selected by the index, clears their pointer fields and the record's first field. It returns the result of the second release when there was one.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1DD4
name: reset_slot_table_state
description: When the mode argument is not 1 it runs two 64-step wait loops. Unless the mode is 2 it then clears all 64 table entries, freeing those with a nonzero second field, and resets the counters and the timeout value to 120.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:1E62
name: load_signed_record_file
description: Optionally opens a named file, checks a four-byte signature, and reads a sequence of tagged records, allocating a buffer for each and seeking as needed. It closes the file when it opened one and returns one if any slot ends up in use, otherwise zero.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:ds:8:213E
name: signal_software_interrupt_if_flagged
description: When a global flag byte is nonzero it raises an exec software interrupt through the Cause call; otherwise it returns at once. It is entered from outside the normal flow.

key: darkseed v1.0 (1992)(cyberdreams)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 7)/Darkseed v1.0 (1992)(Cyberdreams)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 7).adf:s/type:0:0136
name: copy_block_then_call_handler
description: When a buffer pointer is supplied, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in the data block into it. It then calls the routine pointer held in the address register to hand control on.

description: Boot block entry that opens a library through exec, and when it is found sets a flag bit on its base and closes it again. It then looks up a resident module, returning zero when that lookup succeeds and minus one otherwise.

name: boot_open_and_find_resident
description: Boot block entry that opens a library through exec, and when it is found sets a flag bit on its base and closes it again. It then looks up a resident module, returning zero when that lookup succeeds and minus one otherwise.

name: copy_block_then_call_handler
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in a data block into the caller's buffer when one is given, then calls the routine pointer in the address register. Its caller is the max-scan and buffer-preparation step.

name: scan_max_and_build_buffer
description: Walks the entry list to find the largest stored value, then sizes and fills a buffer with a counter-based header pattern. It bounces sixteen longwords of state through a callback in both directions and installs a handler pointer before returning.

name: copy_block_then_call_handler
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in a data block into the caller's buffer when one is given, then calls the routine pointer in the address register. Its caller is the max-scan and buffer-preparation step.

name: startup_collect_dos_message
description: Program entry that opens dos.library, looks up its own task, and waits for a startup message. It allocates a state record and returns error code 20 when that allocation fails, otherwise it opens the file named by the startup data in the current directory.

name: restore_saved_state_and_cleanup
description: Swaps the passed parameter into the task's state record and runs whichever cleanup calls the record's fields call for, including closing a library, replying to a message and freeing the record. It then returns the previously saved parameter.

name: launch_named_tool_from_options
description: Checks the arguments for a debug switch, opens the icon and intuition libraries, and starts the named tool. It reports when the tool's resident module cannot be found or the start fails with an error number, and XORs its name string with a fixed key twice, which leaves it unchanged.

name: compare_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. Returns minus one when the first sorts before the second, one when it sorts after, and zero when they are identical.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of pointer and value pairs, allocating an eight-byte node for each pair and storing a value looked up from it in the node. It links the nodes in order and returns the head, stopping early if an allocation or lookup fails.

name: pad_matching_release_name
description: Compares a name buffer against a global string one character at a time, and when the character at a fixed position is a two and the prefix matches, writes dot-and-space padding over the end of the name. It returns without other effect when the global string ends.

name: write_dot_space_padding
description: Writes a period followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes of the buffer, starting at a fixed offset.

name: match_prefix_against_global
description: Advances through the buffer while its bytes match the global string, stopping at the global string's terminator. It only moves the pointer and returns with no other visible effect.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Empty routine that does no work and returns at once, used only as a callback address.

name: forward_call_with_stack_address
description: Forwards its two parameters to another routine together with the address of a stack slot in its own frame, and returns nothing.

name: format_message_and_emit
description: Formats a message into a 140-byte stack buffer through exec's formatting call, measures the resulting text, and passes it on with its length to an output routine when it is nonempty.

name: scan_bit_transitions_and_report
description: Writes a two-digit count into a text line, then scans ranges of 32-bit words bit by bit, counting every place where a bit changes value between neighbours and storing the running totals in the state record. The routines it calls in the loops are unnamed, so only the counters are visible.

name: clear_globals_and_start_program
description: Zeroes a large block of global variables and records the startup value, then runs a setup routine when a flag bit is set. It then calls through the library and either takes a failure path or runs the main routine.

name: allocate_picture_chip_buffers
description: Allocates several chip-memory blocks of fixed sizes and stores their handles in globals, then runs a series of initialization calls and fills a structure with values derived from the arguments. It also refers to the demo picture file name.

name: start_copper_list_from_state
description: Reads the copper list pointer stored in the state block and passes it to the routine that points the copper at a new list and starts it immediately.

name: configure_resources_set_status
description: Calls routines that configure four stored resources with fixed sizes and rates, then stores a constant status word in a global. The interrupt enable register is reached through the called routines.

name: allocate_chip_row_pointer_table
description: Allocates a zeroed chip-memory block and fills an eight-entry table with pointers spaced 144 bytes apart. It then calls a routine and sets two more globals from the table's base entry, 72 bytes apart.

name: store_constant_then_call
description: Stores the constant 399 in a 16-bit global and then calls a routine.

name: call_with_row_table_block
description: Passes the block pointer from a global table slot, together with the constant size of 1152 bytes, to another routine.

name: call_two_global_pointers
description: Calls a routine with the pointer held in one global slot and then with the pointer held in a second global slot.

name: call_library_with_low_word
description: Extracts the low word of its argument and passes it, together with a global value, to a library stub routine.

name: forward_call_without_arguments
description: Calls one routine with no arguments and returns, passing nothing through.

name: match_pair_table_and_call
description: Searches a two-entry global table for the second argument and, on a match, calls a routine with the paired value. It stores the index reached in a global, which is two when nothing matched.

name: swap_globals_and_call
description: Swaps two 32-bit global values, then passes the new contents of both slots to another routine.

name: initialize_graphics_and_intuition_handles
description: Stores a library handle in a global, sets a sentinel value in one of its fields, and obtains two more handles from library calls, each followed by a failure path when the result is zero. It then stores a masked flag taken from the first handle's record.

name: wait_for_code_then_call
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns one, two or three, then passes a global pointer and a record address to another routine.

name: load_pic_and_wait_sync
description: Loads the load.pic file and waits for a completion flag, giving up after 350000 iterations. It then compares two 16-bit position values against fixed ranges and returns a classification code from zero to three.

name: initialize_game_state
description: Installs two callback pointers and sets three 16-bit state values to 75, 50 and zero. It clears a zero-terminated array, initializes sixteen records from a second array, and then loops, toggling a flag and calling routines each pass.

name: advance_coded_track_sequence
description: Runs one step of a byte-coded sequence for sixteen tracks. Depending on each byte's range it draws a digit-style value, updates an event list, or handles two marker codes, calling drawing routines as it goes until the step ends.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Empty routine that does no work and returns at once, used only as a callback address.

name: run_scene_position_loop
description: Fills eighteen 16-bit position entries from a counter reduced modulo eight, then loops drawing them at positions measured from 168. It repeats until a flag byte is set or the state word reaches zero, returning one.

name: fill_short_arrays_modulo
description: Loops for the count given in its argument, filling one 16-bit array with a value from a called routine reduced modulo 13 and offset by 232, and a second array with the same value reduced modulo 9.

name: step_bouncing_positions
description: Advances a set of bouncing values: each velocity gains one, and where the position would fall below zero the velocity is halved, reversed and the position is clamped to zero. It returns the first nonzero velocity it computed.

name: process_demo_pic_sequence
description: Runs the demo.pic presentation, making a series of library and drawing calls and looping while a routine keeps returning nonzero. It checks a stop flag each pass and then updates the stored pointer and flag globals.

name: build_four_buffer_pointer_pairs
description: Computes four pairs of buffer addresses spaced 300 and 32000 bytes apart, passes each pair to a routine with two output slots, and copies the final pair into four globals.

name: read_asset_file_into_buffer
description: Opens the file named in its argument and reads 32000 bytes into the buffer held in a global, copying the result into a second global before closing the file. It returns zero on success and minus one when the file cannot be opened.

name: load_font_and_sprite_assets
description: Loads the font.dat, land0 and sprites0.dat data files one after another, reading fixed byte counts from each into its own buffer, and closes each file after reading.

name: conditional_load_with_params
description: Opens the file named in its first argument and, if the open succeeds, reads 40000 bytes into the buffer passed second and 64 bytes into a global buffer before closing it. Nothing happens when the open fails.

name: rotate_and_combine_word_table
description: Clips the target row range, then reads a table of five-word groups, rotates each group by the low nibble of the position value and combines the rotated words with the destination's interleaved word planes using AND and OR. Rows outside the clip limits are skipped.

name: apply_rotated_mask_to_tiles
description: Clips the row range, then reads five-word mask groups from a table selected by an index, rotates them by the low nibble of the column value and combines them with the destination tiles using AND and OR, repeating for a fixed number of rows.

name: call_and_return_register_pair
description: Calls one routine and returns the values left in its two data registers combined into a single 64-bit result.

name: apply_tile_mask_table
description: Clips the row range, then combines a table entry selected by a global base and an index with the destination words using AND and OR across four word groups. When the horizontal nibble is zero it takes a direct path without rotating.

name: reorder_record_word_fields
description: Repeats 1680 times over a table of twenty-byte records, shifting the 16-bit words of each record along its fields and writing the reassembled 32-bit values back in place.

name: shift_byte_buffer_left_three
description: Shifts each of the 100 bytes at a fixed buffer address left by three bits, in place.

name: scan_grid_positions
description: Walks a ten-by-ten grid, calling a routine with each cell's computed position offset by a stored table value, and makes an extra call when the matching flag byte is set. The table pointer advances as it goes.

name: call_and_return_register_pair
description: Calls one routine and returns the values left in its two data registers combined into a single 64-bit result.

name: set_text_buffer_pointer
description: Stores the address of a global buffer in a global pointer variable and returns.

name: initialize_buffer_from_string
description: Fills an 80-longword area with all-ones and clears the 320 longwords after it, then measures the string at the global text pointer and writes each character's font entry, indexed from the space character and 40 bytes apart, into the buffer.

name: open_library_and_mask_interrupts
description: Allocates a memory block through exec and, when that succeeds, opens a library, reads and closes a file, and writes interrupt-control values into globals. On failure it runs the exec cleanup calls and returns. The pseudo-code is identical to its neighbours, so only this shared setup is evidenced.

name: open_library_and_mask_interrupts
description: Allocates a memory block through exec and, when that succeeds, opens a library, reads and closes a file, and writes interrupt-control values into globals. On failure it runs the exec cleanup calls and returns. The pseudo-code is identical to its neighbours, so only this shared setup is evidenced.

name: stub_pointer_to_library_init
description: One-instruction entry whose recorded pseudo-code is the shared library setup body, so no behaviour specific to this entry is evidenced beyond a call into exec.

name: stub_pointer_to_library_init

name: load_popsam_file_with_errors
description: Opens the dos library and the popsam file, allocates memory and reads and writes through dos, printing a not-enough-memory or cannot-find-file message on failure. It also writes interrupt-control registers.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Empty routine that does no work and returns at once.

name: clear_byte_and_return
description: Clears a byte at a fixed offset from the register pointer and returns the value passed on the stack.

name: disable_interrupts_then_restore
description: Writes a disable mask for the interrupt bits, calls a routine and frees a block through exec, then restores three saved interrupt values and re-enables the saved set with its top two enable bits set.

name: clear_byte_after_mode_calls
description: Calls one routine when the mode byte is ten and another when it is one, then clears the byte at a fixed offset and returns the value passed on the stack.

name: clear_byte_after_mode_one
description: When the mode byte is one it calls a routine, then clears the byte at a fixed offset and returns the value passed on the stack.

name: clear_byte_and_return
description: Clears a byte at a fixed offset from the register pointer and returns the value passed on the stack.

name: clear_byte_and_return
description: Clears a byte at a fixed offset from the register pointer and returns the value passed on the stack.

description: Clears a byte at a fixed offset from the register pointer and returns the value passed on the stack.

name: clear_byte_and_return
description: Clears a byte at a fixed offset from the register pointer and returns the value passed on the stack.

name: acknowledge_interrupt_flag_bit
description: When bit five of a global flag word is set, it writes 255 to a byte, keeps only bit six of the flag word and calls a routine. Interrupt-request registers are touched by the sequence.

name: build_dispatch_tables
description: Reads a table of stream descriptors from a global area and writes computed pointers and constants into the dispatch tables, dividing a fixed constant by each period value. It then sets up the per-channel entries.

name: build_dispatch_tables
description: Reads a table of stream descriptors from a global area and writes computed pointers and constants into the dispatch tables, dividing a fixed constant by each period value. It then sets up the per-channel entries.

name: reset_global_flags
description: Clears one byte and writes the constants fifteen and 255 into global variables, then returns.

name: update_audio_channel_registers
description: For each audio channel whose pending flag is set, loads its sample pointer and length into the custom audio registers. It returns early when the master flag is clear.

name: advance_sound_channel_stream
description: Counts down a sound channel's gate and, when it expires, reads the next event from the channel's byte stream. It stores a length scaled from a table, a volume and the next stream position in the channel state.

name: advance_sound_channel_stream
description: Resumes the sound event decoder for one channel, reading the next stream event and storing its length, volume and stream position in the channel state.

name: load_instrument_pointers_for_channel
description: Looks up the instrument entry selected by the next stream byte and stores pointers to its data in the channel state.

name: start_sound_channel_event
description: Starts a sound event on a channel: scales the first stream byte by a table value, stores the stream position and sets the channel's pitch value to 256 before entering the event loop.

name: decode_next_sound_event
description: Reads the next sound event byte; non-negative values set the channel's length, volume and stream position, and other values are handled as control codes.

name: set_channel_flag_and_decode
description: Stores a stream byte in the channel state, sets bit one of the channel's status byte, and continues decoding events.

name: step_channel_pointer_list
description: Steps through the channel's pointer list, wrapping to the start at a zero entry, and resolves the next data pointer from the base address.

name: program_dma_channel_from_event
description: Scales the event by the channel's stored factor, stores the stream position, and programs the DMA channel's pointer and length registers from the channel table before continuing to decode.

name: run_sound_event_loop
description: Runs the sound event loop for one channel, dispatching on each event byte and updating the channel's stream position and volume until the stream ends.

name: forward_sound_event_decode
description: Short entry point that loads the stream and channel pointers and continues into the sound event decoder.

name: step_sound_channel_period
description: Reads the next value from a channel's stream, updates the channel's period field from it and calls a routine.

name: forward_sound_event_decode
description: Short entry point that loads the stream and channel pointers and continues into the sound event decoder.

name: combine_word_planes
description: Loops over 64 rows of words, combining each word with entries from a global table using AND, OR and NOT, and writes the results to four spaced locations per iteration. It returns a combined register pair.

name: mask_word_planes
description: Loops 160 times over source and destination word arrays, masking each destination word with the source and a global table value using AND, NOT and OR, and updating four spaced planes per iteration.

name: store_stack_word_and_call
description: Copies a word from the caller's stack into a global variable, calls another routine, and returns the values left in its two data registers as one 64-bit result.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls another routine and returns, with no other effect.

name: poll_mouse_and_keyboard_input
description: Polls the mouse port movement and the button register, updating the stored position with the scaled movement clamped to a minimum of zero, and reads the keyboard serial register when the flag is set. It then calls a routine and returns both input registers as one value.

name: split_state_word_and_call
description: Splits a 16-bit global into its low and high bytes, stores each in its own global, and calls another routine.

name: store_state_and_enable_interrupts
description: Copies a global into two storage slots and writes a constant with the top two bits set into the interrupt control global.

name: manage_interrupt_flag
description: When the pending flag is nonzero, writes a disable mask for the low fourteen interrupt bits, copies the pending value into the interrupt control global with the top two enable bits set, and clears the flag. It returns the value held in the global.

name: build_copper_list_entries
description: Writes a sequence of copper list words into the list buffer, including display window start and stop values, with a branch on a global mode flag choosing between two sets. The DMA control register is touched by the caller's sequence.

name: wait_copper_sync
description: Writes a parameter and the parameter plus four to a global, then loops until bit five of that global is set and returns the masked value.

name: wait_for_interrupt_bit
description: Writes the constant 32 to a global and spins until bit five of that global is set, then returns the masked bit.

name: copy_shorts_after_marker
description: Scans a short array for the marker value 384, then copies a counted run of shorts from a source into the array just after the marker.

name: unrecovered_routine_no_pseudocode
description: No pseudo-code was recovered for this routine, so its behaviour cannot be described; the listed facts show one caller and 21 instructions.

name: update_byte_buffer_from_params
description: Looks up a byte buffer pointer in a table using the first argument, then writes several bytes derived from the second argument and a global, setting flag bits conditionally. It returns both input registers as one value.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_key
description: Clears two globals and, when a flag is set, decodes the keyboard serial data into a character through a lookup table covering the number-row symbols, storing it and setting a ready flag. When no key is ready it clears the flag and returns.

name: copy_32000_byte_block
description: Copies 8000 longwords, 32000 bytes, from a source pointer to a destination pointer one longword at a time.

name: decrement_nibble_counters
description: Copies a block of words into a 32-word stack buffer, then repeatedly decrements each nibble until all are zero, waiting on the vertical position register between passes. It calls another routine each pass and once more at the end.

name: call_then_return_result
description: Calls one routine with no arguments, then calls another routine with its two parameters and returns that second result.

name: call_then_conditional_call
description: Calls one routine with its parameter, then calls a second routine only when a global counter is nonzero.

name: store_offset_and_extract_bits
description: Calls a routine, adds the constant 12345 to its result, stores the sum in a global and returns the high 15 bits of the stored value.

name: store_high_word_to_global
description: Stores the high word of its argument in a global variable and returns. Its facts list an exec alert, an old library open and a supervisor call in the wider routine, but the recorded code shows only this store.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Empty routine that does no work and returns at once.

name: setup_dos_streams_from_table
description: Allocates a cleared block sized from a six-byte table entry and returns early on failure. Otherwise it fills the block by querying the dos current directory, input and output and opening a file, calling library stubs along the way.

name: parse_quoted_argument_string
description: Parses a command-line string: it copies the next argument into a buffer, skipping whitespace, and treats double-quoted text as one argument in which doubled quotes stand for a single quote. Each argument is terminated in the buffer and a count global is set.

name: append_string_with_limit
description: Finds the end of the first string and appends the second to it, copying at most 32767 characters and terminating the result.

name: copy_string_with_limit
description: Copies bytes from a source pointer to a destination pointer, stopping at a null terminator or when the counter in the third argument expires. If the counter expires first it writes a null terminator at the next destination byte.

name: copy_string_pad_zeros
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination up to a count or until a null terminator, then fills any remaining count with zeros.

name: multiply_32_bit_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from the data registers using their 16-bit halves and returns the full 64-bit product.

name: open_window_icon_file
description: Opens the WINDOW file through dos and makes a sequence of library calls, including icon library lookups, checking each result for zero before continuing.

name: check_global_flags_and_cleanup
description: Calls the routine pointer held in a global when it is set, then calls another routine.

name: check_global_flags_and_cleanup
